newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRD increases lead in Mexico City race -- poll.
newsitem.headline: PRD increases lead in Mexico City race -- poll.

text.p: A poll released on Wednesday showed the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) increasing its lead in the first-ever vote for mayor of Mexico City on July 6.

The PRD, whose candidate is Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, a twice-failed presidential contender, was favored by 40.1 percent of those polled by the Center of Opinion Studies of the University of Guadalajara, the center said.

His closest rival was the conservative National Action Party, led by candidate is Carlos Castillo Peraza, with 19.8 percent. The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), represented by candidate Alfredo Del Mazo, was third with 17.9 percent.
The poll has shown a dramatic increase in support for the PRD and a freefall for the PAN. In the center's survey in February, the PAN led with 42.9 percent and the PRD was second with 23.5 percent.
The latest poll was conducted from May 31 to June 1 at 60 places in Mexico City among 1,204 people. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 2.83 percent.
Mexico City residents will choose their mayor for the first time ever in the July vote. In the past, the mayor was appointed by the president.
